_what: How an installed macOS app is checked for the hardening it should have (read-data/app-hardening.mjs): the Electron fuses read from the framework binary, the code-signing flags and the entitlements read with the system's codesign, and the bundle's integrity hash against whether the fuse that enforces it is on. `fuse_tables` lists the fuse names in wire order for each wire version (the byte after the sentinel); `expect` says which fuse states and entitlements count as findings. A new fuse version, expectation or entitlement is a row here.

fuses.name: RunAsNode
fuses.why: While on, the app's own signed binary runs any script as Node.

fuses.name: EnableNodeOptionsEnvironmentVariable
fuses.why: While on, NODE_OPTIONS can load code into the signed app.

fuses.name: EnableNodeCliInspectArguments
fuses.why: While on, --inspect opens a debugger on the signed app.

fuses.name: EnableEmbeddedAsarIntegrityValidation
fuses.why: While off, the app's code archive can be edited and still run.

fuses.name: OnlyLoadAppFromAsar
fuses.why: While off, a folder beside the archive can replace the app's code.

fuses.name: EnableCookieEncryption
fuses.why: While off, session cookies sit on disk in the clear.

forbidden_entitlements.name: com.apple.security.cs.disable-library-validation
forbidden_entitlements.why: Any library may be loaded into the app, signed or not.

forbidden_entitlements.name: com.apple.security.cs.allow-dyld-environment-variables
forbidden_entitlements.why: DYLD variables can inject code into the app.

forbidden_entitlements.name: com.apple.security.get-task-allow
forbidden_entitlements.why: Another process may attach to and control the app.

forbidden_entitlements.name: com.apple.security.cs.debugger
forbidden_entitlements.why: The app may debug other apps.

words.no_electron: {app} does not carry an Electron framework, so there are no fuses to read.
words.no_sentinel: The Electron framework of {app} carries no fuse block; it is not read.
words.unknown_version: The fuse block of {app} is version {version}, which this check has no table for.
words.not_hardened: {app} is not signed with the hardened runtime.
words.integrity_not_enforced: {app} records an integrity hash for its code archive, but the fuse that enforces it is off, so the hash protects nothing.
words.clean: {app} meets every expectation in the list.
